story.iWant: to control robot axes manually using a PlayStation DualShock 4 controller
story.soThat: I can jog axes, trigger emergency stop, manage brakes and enable states, and quickly return to home positions during testing and setup

tasks.task: Project setup - Create tools/joystick_control/ with requirements.txt and config.yaml
Serial communication module - Configurable port/baudrate, send_command(), reconnection
Joystick input module - pygame init, DualShock 4 detection, button/hat events
Startup sequence - MODE query, set READY, query brake status
Axis jog control - VEL/STOP commands, R2 modifier for direction
E-STOP function - Share button sends TEST ESTOP immediately
Home position management - Save via POS, restore via MOVE
Brake control - D-pad Left + axis button toggles BRAKE
Enable control - D-pad Up + axis button toggles EN + POSOK
Status table display - ASCII table with enable/brake per axis
Safety/error handling - Disconnect detection, Ctrl+C graceful exit

acceptanceCriteria.ac: Script connects to ESP32 via configurable serial port (default /dev/ttyUSB0, 115200 baud)
Script connects to DualShock 4 controller via Bluetooth using pygame
On startup, script queries mode via MODE and sets to READY if in IDLE
Pressing axis button (0-6) sends VEL {axis} {speed} command
Releasing axis button sends STOP {axis} command
Holding R2 (modifier) + axis button sends negative speed value
Pressing Share button sends TEST ESTOP command immediately
Pressing Touchpad queries positions via POS and saves to YAML config
Pressing Options moves all axes sequentially to saved home positions
Script handles serial disconnect gracefully (stops all axes, shows error)
Script handles joystick disconnect gracefully (stops all axes, shows error)
Ctrl+C sends STOP to all axes before exiting
Console shows real-time feedback of commands sent and responses received
On startup, script queries brake status for all servo axes (X, Y, Z, A, B) via BRAKE {axis}
D-pad Left + axis button toggles brake state via BRAKE {axis} 0/1
D-pad Up + axis button toggles enable state via EN {axis} 0/1
When enabling axis, script also sends POSOK {axis} to clear position loss
Status table displays current enable and brake state for all axes
Status table updates after each state change

docs.doc: USB CDC serial interface at 115200 baud, text commands (MOVE, MOVR, VEL, STOP, etc.), command response within 10ms
Hardware E-stop with immediate motor shutdown, brake control with configurable strategies
Motors disabled by default, smooth acceleration on VEL change, brake timing ~50us software path
VEL X 0.030 for jog at 30mm/s, POS X returns position, MOVE for absolute positioning

file.reason: Defines all command strings (CMD_VEL, CMD_STOP, CMD_BRAKE, CMD_EN, CMD_POS, CMD_MODE, CMD_POSOK) and response formats
file.symbols: CMD_VEL, CMD_STOP, CMD_BRAKE, CMD_EN, CMD_POS, CMD_MODE, CMD_POSOK, CMD_MOVE, CMD_RST, CMD_TEST, RESP_OK, RESP_ERROR, MODE_NAME_IDLE, MODE_NAME_READY, MODE_NAME_ESTOP

file.reason: VEL command implementation - shows velocity parameter handling and response format
BRAKE command - shows query (BRAKE X) returns 'ENGAGED/RELEASED', set (BRAKE X 0/1)
POSOK command to clear position loss
MODE command handling and state management

dependencies.note: This is a host-side Python tool, not ESP32 firmware. No ESP-IDF dependencies.

constraints.constraint: Motors disabled by default at power-on - requires explicit EN command
Only axes X, Y, Z, A, B have brake hardware; C, D have no brakes
VEL command uses max_acceleration from config by default
TEST ESTOP triggers emergency stop, requires RST to clear
Position unknown after E-STOP - all axes marked UNHOMED
Tool is host-side Python, NOT firmware modification
Speed values per axis defined in story: X=4, Y=1, Z=2, A=1, B=1, C=2, D=2 mm/s

interface.name: DualShock 4 Pygame
interface.hat: joystick.get_hat(0) returns (x, y): Left=(-1,0), Up=(0,1), Right=(1,0), Down=(0,-1)

tests.standards: This is a Python host tool - use pytest for unit tests. Mock serial communication for testing command/response handling. Test joystick input handling with pygame mock or integration tests with real controller.

ideas.idea: Test serial connection with mock port, verify reconnection on disconnect
Test button press sends VEL, release sends STOP
Test R2 modifier inverts velocity sign
Test Share button sends TEST ESTOP immediately
Test POS parsing and YAML save/load for home positions
Test D-pad Left modifier toggles brake correctly
Test D-pad Up modifier sends EN then POSOK
